qc/runs/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r13/raw-evidence-index.json (hashes of run_golden.sh and all results/*.json and *.png recomputed and matching)
evidence:
WHAT IS RIGHT (most of the row). No sibling-task residue: grep of task/tests, instruction.md and the notes for sign-in/account/tenant/forged/password/CHANGE_ME/other product names finds only this task's own no-account statements; the template's sign-in, forged-request and tenant-isolation paragraphs were removed from all five prompts. tests/app_context.md:3-14 describes this app accurately: 'Name: Colderwater playground', 'URL: http://localhost:3000', 'Accounts: None. The app has no sign-in' (matches instruction.md:5 'without signing in', overview.md:3 'without accounts', policy.md:3), entities 'saved snippets with revision history' and '.js or .html' filename mode (overview.md:3), and a single Key screen at / listing title and filename fields, editor with Undo, Redo, Format, Find and Replace, line and column readout, Run, Stop, New, Save, preview, console, library and revision history, all of which are public in ui.md:5-17 and all visible in the golden screenshot golden-1440-history.png. Health address in app_context.md:24 equals integration.md:3 'GET /api/health'. Cross-references inside the prompts resolve: constraints prompt 'the browser-storage clearing that the second criterion asks for' = cw_shared_saved_record (second criterion of gates/constraints/judge.toml); functional prompt 'the three uses named in the application notes' = app_context.md:26; 'One criterion also uses a public https address' and 'the preview-isolation criterion' = cw_preview_isolation; 'Only the criterion that names it may call the restart_app tool' = cw_save_reload_restart only; the scored-prompt browser gate ('text typed into the code editor appears in it') matches the render gate criterion; visual prompt's ten-line draft, caret and double-click selection match cw_visual_editor_readability.

DEFECT 1 (prompt contradicts its own criteria). tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:20: 'Do not penalize which colours the app chose; judge only whether they are used consistently.' But tests/scored/visual/judge.toml:24 (cw_visual_editor_readability) tells the judge to 'assess the rendered editor's typography, line-number alignment with their lines, text contrast and the visibility of the caret and of a selection', and judge.toml:56 (cw_visual_component_finish) to 'assess the colour harmony, consistency of buttons and fields'. Text contrast and colour harmony are both judgements about which colours were chosen, not about whether they are used consistently, so the prompt forbids what two of the three criteria ask for.

DEFECT 2 (shared context loosens one criterion). tests/app_context.md:21: 'A selection can be confirmed by copying it with the usual shortcut and pasting it into an ordinary field such as Find, or by reading the highlighted text.' tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:56 (cw_mouse_selection): 'Confirm each selection by copying it with the usual keyboard shortcut and comparing the copied text ... Fails if ... nothing is copied, or if only a highlight is drawn while the copied text is empty or different.' The context offers highlight reading as a sufficient alternative for every dimension; this criterion says highlight alone is a failure.

NOTES (not counted as defects). (a) Prompts and criteria refer to 'the application notes' (constraints prompt.md:5, functional prompt.md:20, criteria cw_shared_saved_record, cw_save_reload_restart, cw_preview_isolation, cw_history_restore_retry) but the injected section is headed '## Notes for grading' (app_context.md:16); a judge can infer it, the label is just not the same. (b) The product name 'Colderwater' appears in every prompt's first line and in app_context but nowhere in instruction.md or the notes; no criterion requires the name to be shown, so it is not graded. (c) app_context.md:25 says 'where a criterion says to clear browser storage first' while both criteria clear it mid-flow ('Then clear this origin's browser storage').

EVIDENCE LIMITS. This is a source reading. No configured judge run exists for these bytes (raw-evidence-index.json scope line); the scripted golden run does not read the prompts, and the hosted run was on an earlier candidate and only on the golden and a dead app, so neither defect has been exercised by a judge. app_context.md:19 relies on a 'Playwright code runner (page.mouse and page.keyboard)' in @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 (tests/Dockerfile:19) with no vision capability in the judge args; I could not verify that tool list locally.
counterexample: Defect 1: a conforming app whose code text is uniformly dim grey on a dark grey background, or whose buttons and panels use a clashing but consistently applied palette. A judge following prompt.md:20 must not lower the score for the chosen colours and gives 5; a judge following the criterion text lowers cw_visual_editor_readability for 'text contrast' (anchor 2 'code is hard to read') and cw_visual_component_finish for 'colour harmony'. Same app, up to three Likert points apart on each of two of the three visual criteria, about 0.08 of total reward. Defect 2: a broken app that draws a selection highlight on double click, triple click and drag but whose copy shortcut copies nothing (ui.md:7 requires 'Copying a selection with the usual keyboard shortcut should work'). A judge using the app_context.md:21 alternative 'or by reading the highlighted text' passes cw_mouse_selection although the criterion says that case fails.
suggested_fix: Visual prompt.md:20: scope the sentence to palette taste, for example 'Do not penalize the palette the app chose as a matter of taste; readable contrast and consistent use are still judged as the criteria describe', and either drop 'colour harmony' from cw_visual_component_finish or reword it to consistent colour use so the description matches its own anchors. app_context.md:21: say that highlight reading is acceptable only where a criterion allows it and that a criterion asking for the copied text needs the copy. Optionally rename the heading or the references so 'application notes' and '## Notes for grading' are one label.
